results.summary: This project implements multiple free-running oscillators to compare simulation results with reality, and also includes a true random number generator (TRNG). The design uses combinational loops with dividers to reduce output frequencies to below 50kHz. Users can select different clock sources via input pins and measure the generated clock frequencies on the outputs, while the TRNG output can be observed on a dedicated pin. It serves as a test for oscillator behavior and random number generation.

This project is a configurable PWM generator designed to produce PWM signals with incremental duty cycles based on three digital input signals. The duty cycle will increment by 12.5% for each input combination, ranging from 12.5% to 100%. Testing requires an external signal generator for the 10MHz clock and an oscilloscope to visualize the pulse width variations. It is intended for applications requiring easy PWM configuration.

This project uses an OR gate configuration to generate the letter 'J' on a seven-segment LED display. The design is implemented in Wokwi and operates at a 10kHz clock frequency. Testing involves manipulating input switches to form the desired character on the display. No specific external hardware is listed beyond the seven-segment display itself.

This design implements Wolfram's Rule 30 cellular automaton, a chaotic system known for its pseudo-random behavior, and renders it to a VGA monitor. A 320-bit register stores the automaton's state, updating all cells in parallel for each of the 480 displayed rows, resulting in a characteristic triangular chaos pattern. The design requires a VGA monitor connected via a Tiny VGA Pmod and allows users to cycle through different color palettes using input pins. It demonstrates a hardware implementation of complex emergent behavior.

This project is a simple analog buffer implemented using two inverters, one large and one small, connected in series. It originates from Matt's analog course and serves as a basic test of analog circuit behavior. The analog input is provided on pin ua[1] and the output is available on pin ua[0]. No external hardware is required for testing this fundamental analog building block.

This is a switch puzzle game designed to control a seven-segment display, where each input switch toggles its corresponding segment and its neighbors. The objective is to illuminate the display to show all numbers from 0 to 9. Testing requires connecting microswitches to the inputs and a seven-segment display to the outputs. The project is implemented in Wokwi and is intended as an educational puzzle.

This project generates a controllable Archimedes spiral pattern (r=theta) and displays it using VGA output. It requires a PMOD VGA adapter for connection to a monitor and operates at a 25 MHz clock frequency. Input pins can be used to alter the foreground/background colors and the speed of the spiral animation. Optional switches can provide further control over the pattern.

This design implements an octal classifier that recognizes images of numbers from 0 to 7 using their 16 most significant pixels. The input features are provided via digital pins, and the classification result is displayed on a seven-segment display. Testing involves setting the input features according to the pixel data of the number image to be classified. The project aims to demonstrate a hardware-based image classification capability.

NeuroPulse is a 4-neuron spiking neural network (SNN) accelerator based on the Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) model, designed to operate with weights stored off-chip on an RP2040. It processes neurons sequentially, achieving high simulation speeds for biological processes. The design includes per-neuron state tracking and supports Hebbian learning for weight updates. Testing can be performed with or without the RP2040, using input pins for spike injection and monitoring output pins for spike events and FSM status.

This project aims to implement a counter that increments every second, displaying the count on a seven-segment display. The design is intended for testing purposes, potentially involving input skew measurement. However, the 'How it works' and 'How to test' sections are currently incomplete. External hardware such as programmable delay lines on the inputs is suggested for testing.
